x-k-k10-01.title: One idiom, two different feelings.
x-k-k10-01.goal: Infer the shared figurative meaning of 손이 크다 from 3 sentences, decide where e sound like complaint, and quote Korean evidence to explain the different feelings.
x-k-k10-01.material:
Three people talk about somebody. Same expression 손이 크다 show every time (we no explain am here).
(가) 엄마는 손이 커서 김장할 때마다 이웃 몫까지 넉넉하게 담그세요.
(나) 동생은 손이 커서 월급날이면 친구들에게 밥을 사다가 월말에는 늘 빠듯해요.
(다) 새 요리사는 손이 커서 찌개를 끓이면 늘 열 명 분이 나와서 매번 반이 남아요.
x-k-k10-01.thinking.0: Guess idiom meaning from different contexts.
x-k-k10-01.thinking.1: Separate core meaning from the feeling it carries.
x-k-k10-01.prereq.0: Can read Korean sentences with -아서/-어서 and -(으)ㄹ 때마다.
x-k-k10-01.prereq.1: Know Korean has fixed expressions whose meaning no be just the sum of each word.
x-k-k10-01.s.s1.prompt: Which main meaning of 손이 크다 fit all 3 sentences?
x-k-k10-01.s.s1.hint.0: Hide the idiom and ask what the 3 situations (김장, 월급날, 찌개) have in common.
x-k-k10-01.s.s1.hint.1: Test each option with all 3 sentences, no just the easiest one.
x-k-k10-01.s.s1.o.a: The person get physically big hands wey help for kitchen.
x-k-k10-01.s.s1.r.a: Taking the words literally. Check (나): salary and treating friends no relate to hand size.
x-k-k10-01.s.s1.o.b: The person na skilled cook wey make tasty food anywhere.
x-k-k10-01.s.s1.r.b: You focus only on (가) and (다). Check (나): no cooking there, so meaning must be wider than cooking.
x-k-k10-01.s.s1.o.c: The person dey spend money without thinking about tomorrow.
x-k-k10-01.s.s1.r.c: This fit (나) only. Check (가) and (다): dem talk about food amount, no careless spending.
x-k-k10-01.s.s1.o.d: The person handle food, money or gifts with plenty generosity.
x-k-k10-01.s.s1.r.d: Build a meaning wey fit all 3 contexts, no just the first one.
x-k-k10-01.s.s1.explain: For all 3, 손이 크다 describe person wey use, give or make things plenty. Cooking and money na just the situations.
x-k-k10-01.s.s2.prompt: In which sentences speaker treat 손이 크다 like small problem? Choose all wey apply.
x-k-k10-01.s.s2.hint.0: For each sentence, how the speaker sound: happy, neutral or worried?
x-k-k10-01.s.s2.hint.1: Then find the words wey give you that feeling.
x-k-k10-01.s.s2.r.a: Read 넉넉하게 / 이웃 몫까지 as warm detail, no complaint. No bad result in this sentence.
x-k-k10-01.s.s2.r.b: Notice result clause 빠듯해요 (money tight): same habit now sound like worry.
x-k-k10-01.s.s2.r.c: Notice 매번 반이 남아요 (half remain every time) as bad result.
x-k-k10-01.s.s2.explain: Core meaning of idiom neutral. Feeling come from result: 빠듯해요 and 반이 남아요 show problem, but 넉넉하게 in (가) sound friendly.
x-k-k10-01.s.s3.prompt: In English or Korean, explain why same idiom feel warm in (가) but worrying in (나). Quote at least one Korean phrase as evidence.
x-k-k10-01.s.s3.hint.1: Say wetin stay same (idiom) and wetin change (outcome).
x-k-k10-01.s.s3.selfAssess.0: I say what remain same and what change?
x-k-k10-01.s.s3.selfAssess.1: I point to the exact words carrying the feeling?
x-k-k10-01.s.s3.selfAssess.2: Could classmate find my evidence in the text?
x-k-k10-01.s.s3.model.0: In (가), 이웃 몫까지 넉넉하게 show sharing, so generosity get praise. In (나), same habit lead to 월말에는 늘 빠듯해요, so result na money problem. Idiom same; result clause change the feeling.
x-k-k10-01.s.s3.model.1: 손이 크다 just mean she/he use things plenty. In (가) e help neighbours, but in (나) 빠듯해요 show brother spend too much, so speaker sound worried.
x-k-k10-01.s.s3.model.2: (가) 넉넉하게 담그세요 na gift to neighbours, so warm; (나) 월말에는 늘 빠듯해요 na money wahala, so worry.

x-k-k10-02.title: Read headline and check its numbers.
x-k-k10-02.goal: Find the sentence in short news article wey claim more than evidence support. Rewrite headline to match data and mention survey limit.
x-k-k10-02.material:
Headline: 서울 시민 다수, 대중교통 요금 인상 찬성
(Read the headline first, then the article 4 sentences, numbered 1 to 4.)
x-k-k10-02.thinking.0: Check a claim against the figures.
x-k-k10-02.thinking.1: Notice when sample no represent everyone.
x-k-k10-02.prereq.0: Can read percentages and numbers in Korean news.
x-k-k10-02.prereq.2: Know 다수 (many/most) and 과반 (more than half).
x-k-k10-02.s.s1.prompt: Which sentence claim more than earlier sentences support?
x-k-k10-02.s.s1.hint.0: Compare percentages in sentence 2 with conclusion in last sentence.
x-k-k10-02.s.s1.hint.1: Before deciding who they represent, ask who the 1,000 people actually were.
x-k-k10-02.s.s1.explain: Line 4 overstates it. 다수 sound like most, but 48% less than half, and 41% oppose. 찬성 na biggest group (plurality), no majority. Line 3 also show only people met at subway stations during rush hour answer, so no speak for all Seoul residents.
x-k-k10-02.s.s2.prompt: Rewrite headline in Korean to fit the numbers, and add one Korean or English sentence naming a survey limit.
x-k-k10-02.s.s2.hint.0: Use actual numbers in line 2 instead of vague word.
x-k-k10-02.s.s2.hint.1: Check line 3 for a survey limitation.
x-k-k10-02.s.s2.selfAssess.0: My headline say only what 48% and 41% support?
x-k-k10-02.s.s2.selfAssess.1: My limit concern who they ask, not the topic?
x-k-k10-02.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Could my headline mislead reader into thinking “all citizens”?

x-k-k10-03.title: Does library use cause higher grades?
x-k-k10-03.goal: Choose extra information wey fit test whether library use cause higher grades, catch reversed-cause thinking, and write one researcher question.
x-k-k10-03.material: News summary: 한 연구에서 한 달에 도서관을 8번 이상 이용한 학생의 평균 성적이 2번 미만 이용한 학생보다 높았다. 연구자는 "도서관 이용이 성적을 올린다"고 말했다.
x-k-k10-03.thinking.1: Choose information wey fit settle the claim.
x-k-k10-03.prereq.0: Can read short Korean news summary.
x-k-k10-03.s.s1.prompt: Which extra facts help you decide whether library use CAUSE higher grades? Choose all wey apply.
x-k-k10-03.s.s1.hint.0: For each choice, ask if answer fit change how likely library be the cause.
x-k-k10-03.s.s1.hint.1: Ask wetin else differ between frequent and rare library users.
x-k-k10-03.s.s1.o.a: Whether same students grades were measured before and after they start using library often.
x-k-k10-03.s.s1.r.a: Track changes in same people over time; one-time comparison no show this.
x-k-k10-03.s.s1.o.b: Which kinds of books students borrow most often.
x-k-k10-03.s.s1.r.b: Interesting use detail, but no show whether library or something else cause grades.
x-k-k10-03.s.s1.o.c: Whether frequent library users already study more or have more motivation.
x-k-k10-03.s.s1.r.c: Look for a third factor wey fit explain both library use and grades.
x-k-k10-03.s.s1.o.d: Average grade for all students in the country.
x-k-k10-03.s.s1.r.d: National average show whether these students typical, not what cause their score gap.
x-k-k10-03.s.s1.o.e: Whether grades come from school records or students own reports.
x-k-k10-03.s.s1.r.e: Check reliability of grades; this help assess claim generally, though no directly show cause.
x-k-k10-03.s.s1.explain: To test cause, need before/after results for same students (a), plus check other factors like study time or motivation (c). Book types and national average no address cause.
x-k-k10-03.s.s1.acc.0: Checking how grades were measured (e) reasonable, because it tests data reliability, even if no directly address cause.
x-k-k10-03.s.s2.prompt: Reader say, “Maybe students with high grades like studying, so dem go library more.” Which idea this show?
x-k-k10-03.s.s2.hint.0: Compare study claim with reader idea: in each one, which thing cause and which one result?
x-k-k10-03.s.s2.hint.1: Choose the option about direction, not honesty or sampling.
x-k-k10-03.s.s2.r.a: You jump to accuse study; reader idea concern direction, not honesty.
x-k-k10-03.s.s2.o.b: Library use and grades definitely no relate.
x-k-k10-03.s.s2.r.b: You overcorrect: reverse direction no mean connection no dey.
x-k-k10-03.s.s2.o.c: Cause fit go the other way: high grades (or study habit) fit lead to more library use.
x-k-k10-03.s.s2.r.c: Consider reverse direction of cause and effect.
x-k-k10-03.s.s2.o.d: Only students wey like reading answer survey.
x-k-k10-03.s.s2.r.d: You mix in sampling worry wey reader sentence no mention.
x-k-k10-03.s.s2.explain: Reader suggest reverse causation. Same figures fit support both directions, so claim that library use raise grades go beyond data.
x-k-k10-03.s.s3.prompt: In Korean, write ONE question you would ask researcher before accepting “도서관 이용이 성적을 올린다.”
x-k-k10-03.s.s3.hint.0: Choose missing fact from step 1 or reverse direction from step 2.
x-k-k10-03.s.s3.hint.1: Think what you need to know to rule out another explanation.
x-k-k10-03.s.s3.selfAssess.0: My question point to missing information, no just show doubt?
x-k-k10-03.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Could the answer change my judgment?

x-k-k10-04.title: Reading “oh, okay…”
x-k-k10-04.topic: Tone and implied meaning in chat.
x-k-k10-04.goal: Update how you read coworker reply as more chat appear, and explain which Korean phrases change your mind.
x-k-k10-04.material: Team chat at Korean company. 지민 na newest member; 선배 na senior colleague. Chat appear in 3 parts.
x-k-k10-04.thinking.0: Read the meaning behind polite words.
x-k-k10-04.thinking.1: Update judgment when new evidence come.
x-k-k10-04.prereq.1: Know 괜찮아 and 알겠습니다 fit be said without happy agreement.
x-k-k10-04.s.s1.prompt: Read each chat part. Each time, choose the most reasonable idea about 지민 feeling.
x-k-k10-04.s.s1.hint.0: Ask what they say directly and what they only hint at.
x-k-k10-04.s.s1.hint.1: After each new part, check whether your earlier idea still fit.
x-k-k10-04.s.s1.st.0.after: So far, only hesitation show. 네 can mean “I hear you”; opening 아 and ending … suggest discomfort.
x-k-k10-04.s.s1.st.0.r.a: You read 네 as excitement and ignore trailing 아 and …
x-k-k10-04.s.s1.st.0.r.b: You read refusal into a word wey literally mean yes.
x-k-k10-04.s.s1.st.0.o.c: She hear the question and hesitate; she no clearly volunteer.
x-k-k10-04.s.s1.st.0.r.c: Notice 네 here answer “I hear you,” not “I will do it.”
x-k-k10-04.s.s1.st.1.ask: How you go read her answer now?
x-k-k10-04.s.s1.st.1.after: 알겠습니다 mean she accept task, but 제가요? and pause show surprise and reluctance. She comply; that no mean she happy to agree.
x-k-k10-04.s.s1.st.1.o.a: She delighted and thanking the senior.
x-k-k10-04.s.s1.st.1.r.a: You treat formal 알겠습니다 as warm enthusiasm.
x-k-k10-04.s.s1.st.1.o.b: She go do am, but she no happy.
x-k-k10-04.s.s1.st.1.r.b: See 알겠습니다 as compliance, while 제가요? show surprise.
x-k-k10-04.s.s1.st.1.r.c: You miss that 알겠습니다 accept the request.
x-k-k10-04.s.s1.st.2.info: Later, 지민 message friend: “자료 정리? 뭐, 어차피 내가 제일 막내인데 어쩌겠어. 괜찮아.”
x-k-k10-04.s.s1.st.2.ask: Suppose senior see what she write to friend. What be the best next step?
x-k-k10-04.s.s1.st.2.after: 어쩌겠어 mean she feel no real choice, and 막내 explain why. 괜찮아 here sound like she closing topic, no comfort.
x-k-k10-04.s.s1.st.2.o.a: Offer to share the work or help, and check how she dey.
x-k-k10-04.s.s1.st.2.r.a: Notice 어쩌겠어 and 막내 signal a one-sided burden.
x-k-k10-04.s.s1.st.2.o.b: Thank her nicely in team chat and leave it there.
x-k-k10-04.s.s1.st.2.r.b: Kind, but that assumes she fine and ignores the one-sided burden she describe with 어쩌겠어.
x-k-k10-04.s.s1.reflect: Same words, 네 and 괜찮아, get different weight each time. Pauses like 아… and phrases like 어쩌겠어 carry meaning wey polite words no talk.
x-k-k10-04.s.s2.prompt: For English or Korean, explain how your reading change from first part to last. Quote at least two Korean phrases wey change your mind.
x-k-k10-04.s.s2.hint.0: Name your first interpretation, then quote phrase wey make you change am.
x-k-k10-04.s.s2.hint.1: Choose phrases from different parts of di chat.
x-k-k10-04.s.s2.selfAssess.0: I talk wetin I think at first?
x-k-k10-04.s.s2.selfAssess.1: I connect di change to specific phrases?
x-k-k10-04.s.s2.model.0: At first I read ‘아, 네…’ as simple yes, but ‘제가요?’ show surprise and reluctance, and later ‘어쩌겠어’ tell me she agree only because she be youngest. So ‘괜찮아’ no mean say she dey okay.
x-k-k10-04.s.s2.model.1: My view change after 제가요? and 어쩌겠어. Polite words like 알겠습니다 hide how she feel, and at di end 괜찮아 na her way to end di topic.

x-k-k10-05.title: Late homework, polite message
x-k-k10-05.goal: Judge wetin no proper for text to professor, then rewrite am to ask permission, say who write am, and give reason.
x-k-k10-05.material:
Student send this KakaoTalk message to professor by 11 p.m. (ㅎㅎ na chat short form for laughing, pronounced ‘hieut hieut’; ~ add light friendly tone.)

‘교수님 과제 내일 낼게요 ㅎㅎ 몸이 좀 안 좋아서요. 확인 부탁해요~’
x-k-k10-05.s.s1.prompt: Which parts of this message Korean professor probably find inappropriate? Choose all wey apply.
x-k-k10-05.s.s1.hint.0: Imagine say you be professor reading am by 11 p.m. Wetin you need know?
x-k-k10-05.s.s1.hint.1: Separate wetin message fail to DO (ask, identify writer) from how e only SOUND.
x-k-k10-05.s.s1.o.a: E announce new deadline (‘낼게요’) instead of asking permission
x-k-k10-05.s.s1.r.a: You notice say writer dey decide something wey na professor suppose decide.
x-k-k10-05.s.s1.o.b: Di laughing short form and tilde make di tone casual
x-k-k10-05.s.s1.r.b: Notice language markers wey fit friends better than professor.
x-k-k10-05.s.s1.o.c: Writer no talk who dem be or which class dem dey.
x-k-k10-05.s.s1.r.c: You see say professor fit teach many students and no know who write am.
x-k-k10-05.s.s1.o.d: Message give sickness as reason for delay
x-k-k10-05.s.s1.r.d: Treating a reason like fault, even though reason na exactly wetin people expect.
x-k-k10-05.s.s1.o.e: E use -요 ending instead of more formal -습니다
x-k-k10-05.s.s1.r.e: Judge endings: -요 polite; formal ending good extra, but no be main problem here.
x-k-k10-05.s.s1.explain: Main problems na writer announce instead of ask (a) and no identify self (c). Casual markers (b) and -요 ending (e) fit be debated, while giving reason (d) na good practice.
x-k-k10-05.s.s1.acc.0: Many readers also think symbols too casual for professor; reasonable extra point.
x-k-k10-05.s.s1.acc.1: People expect more formal ending in written message to professor, so noticing am make sense.
x-k-k10-05.s.s1.acc.2: Noticing casual markers and ending, besides two main problems, na reasonable extra.
x-k-k10-05.s.s2.prompt: Rewrite message in Korean (2-4 sentences) for professor. Keep reason, ask permission, and say who you be.
x-k-k10-05.s.s2.hint.0: Start with greeting and your name or class.
x-k-k10-05.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Whole message use respectful language throughout?

x-k-k10-06.title: Idiom wey contradict its sentence
x-k-k10-06.goal: Find sentence where idiom clash with rest, choose correction, then correct another clashing sentence yourself.
x-k-k10-06.material: Learner write four sentences for class blog and use idiom in each. (Idioms: 발등에 불이 떨어지다 = face urgent problem; 누워서 떡 먹기 = very easy; 발이 넓다 = know many people; 소문난 잔치에 먹을 것 없다 = hype bigger than reality.)
x-k-k10-06.thinking.0: Find contradiction between idiom and context
x-k-k10-06.thinking.2: Make idiom and context fit together
x-k-k10-06.prereq.0: Know idioms 발등에 불이 떨어지다, 누워서 떡 먹기, 발이 넓다 as vocabulary
x-k-k10-06.s.s1.prompt: One sentence use idiom in way wey contradict rest. Which line?
x-k-k10-06.s.s1.hint.0: Replace idiom in each line with its meaning, then read again.
x-k-k10-06.s.s1.hint.1: Look for result wey no follow from idiom.
x-k-k10-06.s.s1.explain: Line 3 na problem. 발이 넓다 mean know many people, but rest say team leader stay home and no go any gatherings. Other three idioms fit their contexts.
x-k-k10-06.s.s2.prompt: Which correction of line 3 keep idiom and make sentence make sense?
x-k-k10-06.s.s2.hint.0: Ask which options still make sense if 발이 넓다 mean ‘know many people.’
x-k-k10-06.s.s2.hint.1: Remove options wey still take feet literally.
x-k-k10-06.s.s2.r.a: Reading idiom literally as wide feet.
x-k-k10-06.s.s2.r.b: Keep idiom and give result wey match ‘know many people.’
x-k-k10-06.s.s2.r.c: E keep idiom, but result still no follow: knowing many people no reason to avoid people.
x-k-k10-06.s.s2.r.d: Reading idiom literally as wide feet and shoe shopping.
x-k-k10-06.s.s2.explain: Good correction keep 발이 넓다 as ‘know many people’ and add result, like knowing people in different departments. Literal readings (a, d) use words, no be idiom, and c keep di clash.
x-k-k10-06.s.s3.prompt: Another learner write: ‘그 식당은 소문난 잔치에 먹을 것 없다더니 음식이 정말 맛있고 줄도 길어서 매일 가요.’ Idiom clash with rest. Rewrite as ONE Korean sentence so idiom (or another expression) and rest agree, changing as little as possible.
x-k-k10-06.s.s3.hint.0: Decide wetin idiom say about restaurant, then check whether rest of sentence say same thing.
x-k-k10-06.s.s3.hint.1: You fit change rest of sentence to match idiom, or change opening to match rest.
x-k-k10-06.s.s3.selfAssess.0: If I keep idiom, rest of my sentence say the same thing as idiom?

x-k-k10-07.title: Opposed, but no be ‘majority’
x-k-k10-07.goal: Find headline wey claim too much based on poll results, then create three sets of poll results where ‘more people oppose than support’ true but ‘majority oppose’ no true.
x-k-k10-07.material: Newspaper poll 200 people about new policy. Each person answer 찬성 (support), 반대 (oppose) or 모름 (not sure). For this task, 과반 mean more than half of all 200 people asked (so more than 100).
x-k-k10-07.prereq.0: Fit add and compare whole numbers up to 200
x-k-k10-07.s.s1.prompt: Poll find 찬성 60, 반대 90, 모름 50. Which headline claim more than these numbers support?
x-k-k10-07.s.s1.hint.0: For each headline, write down number or share wey need to be true.
x-k-k10-07.s.s1.hint.1: Check each one against 60, 90 and 50 out of 200.
x-k-k10-07.s.s1.r.b: Compare only two answers and leave out di third one.
x-k-k10-07.s.s1.r.c: Treat ‘most’ as ‘more than any other group’ and miss say 90 out of 200 less than half.
x-k-k10-07.s.s1.r.d: Turn numbers into shares of whole group (90, 60, 50 out of 200).
x-k-k10-07.s.s1.explain: 과반 mean more than half. Half of 200 na 100, and 90 less, so headline with 과반 claim too much. Other ones report numbers correctly.
x-k-k10-07.s.s2.prompt: Enter three different poll results (200 people total) where opposed group biggest (more than 찬성 and more than 모름), but no more than 100, with at least 20 supporting and at least 20 answering 모름.
x-k-k10-07.s.s2.hint.0: Choose number opposing first; keep am at 100 or below.
x-k-k10-07.s.s2.hint.1: Then choose smaller numbers for support and 모름 so all three add up to 200.
x-k-k10-07.s.s2.fail.c1: Use whole numbers of people, no negative numbers.
x-k-k10-07.s.s2.fail.c2: Di three numbers must add up to 200.
x-k-k10-07.s.s2.fail.c3: Opposed number must be bigger than support number.
x-k-k10-07.s.s2.fail.c4: Opposition pass half, so e IS majority.
x-k-k10-07.s.s2.fail.c5: At least 20 people must answer 모름.
x-k-k10-07.s.s2.ok.c6: Opposed number bigger than 모름 too, so na biggest group.
x-k-k10-07.s.s2.fail.c6: Opposed number must be bigger than 모름, so e go be biggest group.
x-k-k10-07.s.s2.fail.c7: At least 20 people must support am.
x-k-k10-07.s.s2.explain: For example, 60/90/50 and 70/100/30 both get more people opposed than supporting, but opposition no pass 100. 100 exactly half, no be ‘more than half.’
x-k-k10-07.s.s2.because.prompt: For English or Korean, explain why ‘opposed na biggest group’ no allow headline ‘과반 반대,’ and what work di other two groups do.
x-k-k10-07.s.s2.because.hint.0: Think how many people no oppose am.
x-k-k10-07.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: I say who no dey counted among opposed?
x-k-k10-07.s.s2.because.model.1: More people opposing than supporting no mean majority: if 90 of 200 oppose, 110 people no oppose, many answer 모름 or 찬성.
x-k-k10-07.s.s2.because.model.2: Biggest group mean only plural group; 모름 and 찬성 together fit be as big as 반대 or bigger.

x-k-k10-08.title: ‘I’ll think about it’ mean yes?
x-k-k10-08.topic: Tone and implied meaning at work
x-k-k10-08.goal: Decide what information go help understand unclear workplace reply, then choose follow-up message wey find out without pressure or assumptions.
x-k-k10-08.material: 현우 send proposal to 박 부장님 (department head) by messenger. Reply: ‘좋은 아이디어네요. 한번 생각해 보겠습니다.’ 현우 no know whether na yes, no or maybe.
x-k-k10-08.thinking.1: Choose proof to clear up ambiguity
x-k-k10-08.s.s1.prompt: Which extra information go help 현우 understand di reply? Choose all wey apply.
x-k-k10-08.s.s1.hint.0: Which facts person wey really interested go provide, but person wey dey decline no go?
x-k-k10-08.s.s1.hint.1: Which fact compare this reply with same person earlier replies?
x-k-k10-08.s.s1.o.a: Whether 박 부장님 ask follow-up questions about budget or timetable
x-k-k10-08.s.s1.r.a: Look for sign of real interest, wey polite no rarely include.
x-k-k10-08.s.s1.o.b: Whether dem send message morning or night
x-k-k10-08.s.s1.r.b: Use detail wey tell little about answer.
x-k-k10-08.s.s1.o.c: Whether 박 부장님 usually talk this before approving or declining
x-k-k10-08.s.s1.r.c: Look for speaker own habit, best clue for indirect reply.
x-k-k10-08.s.s1.r.d: Treat ending as signal, even though endings follow rank, not yes or no.
x-k-k10-08.s.s1.o.e: Whether reply come within minutes or after several days
x-k-k10-08.s.s1.r.e: Use speed as weak proof of interest.
x-k-k10-08.s.s1.explain: Follow-up questions (a) and speaker habit (c) tell most about whether reply na soft no. Time of day (b) and ending (d) tell little, and reply speed (e) weak proof only.
x-k-k10-08.s.s1.acc.0: Reply speed (e) weak, but e still reasonable extra proof.
x-k-k10-08.s.s2.prompt: Which follow-up message from 현우 go find answer best without pressure or assumption?
x-k-k10-08.s.s2.hint.0: Imagine say you be 박 부장님: which message you fit answer easiest?
x-k-k10-08.s.s2.hint.1: Check each choice for assuming, demanding or pressing.
x-k-k10-08.s.s2.r.a: Assume say na yes and act like that.
x-k-k10-08.s.s2.r.b: Ask directly and put senior person on the spot.
x-k-k10-08.s.s2.r.c: Offer help and make space for clear answer without pressure.
x-k-k10-08.s.s2.r.d: Set deadline, wey fit feel like pressure on senior person.
x-k-k10-08.s.s2.explain: Option c dey protect the senior dignity, offer help and ask for more information. a assume yes, b too direct, d dey pressure.

x-k-k10-09.goal: Find the phrase for reply to team leader wey inappropriate by itself, then rewrite whole reply to decline politely.
x-k-k10-09.material: Team leader post for group chat: “이번 금요일 6시 팀 회식입니다. 다들 참석 바랍니다.” New employee get family appointment that evening. Their draft reply:
x-k-k10-09.s.s1.prompt: One phrase for draft na known problem when speaking to senior, no matter the refusal. Which line get am?
x-k-k10-09.s.s1.hint.0: Ask for each line: e go be problem to say am to senior in ANY message, apart from refusing?
x-k-k10-09.s.s1.hint.1: Separate lines wey only blunt for this situation from phrase wey wrong for any message.
x-k-k10-09.s.s1.explain: Line 4 na problem. Koreans dey use 수고하세요 to person same or lower rank; to senior, many prefer 먼저 가보겠습니다 or 고생하셨습니다. Line 2 too blunt (못 가요), but soften refusal; 수고하세요 wrong regardless of refusal.
x-k-k10-09.s.s2.prompt: Rewrite reply in Korean (2-4 sentences): acknowledge notice, politely refuse with reason, and show goodwill.
x-k-k10-09.s.s2.hint.0: Thank or acknowledge first, then apologise before refusing.
x-k-k10-09.s.s2.hint.1: Replace “못 가요” with softer way to say e hard to attend.
x-k-k10-09.s.s2.selfAssess.0: The refusal get respect and reason?
x-k-k10-09.s.s2.selfAssess.2: E sound like person wey still value team?

x-k-k10-10.title: Write sentence wey explain idiom
x-k-k10-10.goal: Choose sentence wey context teach idiom, then write your own sentence with idiom and identify clue and possible wrong reading.
x-k-k10-10.material: Idioms: 귀가 얇다 (people fit sway you easily), 입이 무겁다 (keep secret), 눈이 높다 (high standards, picky). Good example sentence let reader infer meaning from situation.
x-k-k10-10.thinking.2: Think ahead about possible wrong reading
x-k-k10-10.prereq.0: Know the three idioms from meanings.
x-k-k10-10.prereq.1: Fit write Korean sentence with two clauses.
x-k-k10-10.s.s1.prompt: Which sentence help reader infer 귀가 얇다 meaning without explanation?
x-k-k10-10.s.s1.hint.0: Hide idiom and ask wetin reader fit still learn about 민지.
x-k-k10-10.s.s1.hint.1: Remove sentences wey fit be true if her ears just thin.
x-k-k10-10.s.s1.r.a: Adding facts wey no relate, so reader no fit infer anything.
x-k-k10-10.s.s1.r.b: Give behaviours wey show she dey swayed, and reason clause wey connect dem.
x-k-k10-10.s.s1.r.c: Repeating idiom without situation; e explain nothing.
x-k-k10-10.s.s1.r.d: Make context support literal meaning of ears.
x-k-k10-10.s.s1.explain: Option b show action (buying because of advert, changing mind after friends object) wey reveal meaning. a add irrelevant detail, c repeat itself, d support literal reading.
x-k-k10-10.s.s2.prompt: Choose ONE of the three idioms and write two Korean sentences wey let reader wey never see am infer meaning from situation.
x-k-k10-10.s.s2.hint.0: Show wetin person do or wetin happen, no be definition.
x-k-k10-10.s.s2.hint.1: Connect situation to idiom with reason clause.
x-k-k10-10.s.s2.selfAssess.0: If idiom hide, reader fit guess meaning?
x-k-k10-10.s.s2.selfAssess.1: My sentences fit literal reading too?
x-k-k10-10.s.s3.prompt: For English, name exact Korean words in your sentences wey give meaning away, and say how reader fit still misunderstand idiom (for example, literally).
x-k-k10-10.s.s3.hint.0: Quote the clause wey carry the clue.
x-k-k10-10.s.s3.hint.1: Think about literal meaning of body part.
x-k-k10-10.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Did I quote, no be paraphrase?
x-k-k10-10.s.s3.selfAssess.1: My wrong reading na real possibility?
x-k-k10-10.s.s3.selfAssess.2: The phrase I quote dey inside my sentences?
x-k-k10-10.s.s3.model.0: The clue na 아무에게도 얘기하지 않았다; reader fit still take 입이 무겁다 literally as heavy mouth, but secret context make that unlikely.
x-k-k10-10.s.s3.model.1: 눈이 높아서 + 마음에 드는 사람이 없대요 na clues. Person fit read 눈 as eyesight, but dating context make “high standards” clear.
